messages:
marie: Heads up — MediCore POC (Android app) streaming broke during demo. Client throws JSON.parse errors and then disconnects. Repro on their env every ~12-20s. Can eng advise? cc @tom @luis

 tom: Is this our hosted POC endpoint or self-hosted private? Any proxy in front?

 marie: Hosted on our demo tenant. Customer runs traffic thru their Apigee gateway to our endpoint. They sent a packet capture and Android logs.

 luis: Drop the logs here pls. Quick guess: gateway idle timeouts or buffering causing SSE chunks to split.

 marie: Android stack trace:
```
E/StreamReader: Failed to parse event payload: Unexpected end of input at JSON.parse
E/StreamReader: buffer_len=192 last_chunk="{\"note\":\"Follow-up on meds, presc"
```

 Raw bytes client saw (concatenated):
```
data: {"type":"note","payload":{"pt_id":1001,"note":"Follow-up on meds, presc


data: ription: sent"}
```

 luis: Yup, JSON is split across two SSE events or chunk boundaries. Android parser tries to parse partial payload. Two paths: 1) fix server/gateway so each SSE event is delivered intact and proxy doesn't coalesce/split; 2) make client aggregate event data until full event terminator (double newline) before JSON.parse. For presales/demo, do (1) first.

 tom: On the server side we should ensure: Content-Type: text/event-stream, transfer-encoding: chunked, flush after each event. Also send a heartbeat comment every 8s to keep idle timeouts happy. What are the customer's gateway timeouts?

 marie: Customer sent gateway log: 
```
[2026-11-08T09:14:02Z] upstream idle timeout=15s, worker closed connection
[2026-11-08T09:14:02Z] downstream connection reset by client
```

 sara: 15s idle timeout — emit heartbeat <15s, e.g., every 7-10s. Also add X-Accel-Buffering: no for nginx-based proxies, and disable gzip for the SSE route. Example SSE event pattern we recommend:
```
: heartbeat


data: {"type":"update","payload":{...}}


```
Flush after writes.

 luis: If Apigee is in the path, ensure "Streaming response" is enabled and disable response buffering. Some gateways will gzip and re-chunk which breaks line framing.

 marie: Customer asks if Redwood can inject heartbeat from our side automatically for hosted POCs. Is there a toggle?

 tom: We don't currently auto-insert comment heartbeats for hosted API. We can add per-route keepalive via config, but for POC fastest is to add on the application side or ask customer to lower gateway coalescing. I can open a small internal ticket to add a per-route keepalive flag for hosted POCs.

 ops-bot: :white_check_mark: POC-4567 flagged to eng-platform for "sse-keepalive" feature request.

 marie: For the immediate demo, asking customer to patch their gateway settings + we'll push a short patch to our demo server to flush and send heartbeats. Also advising Android client to buffer until event delimiter.

 luis: One more: if switching to NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) is acceptable for the app, it's more resilient to chunking, but requires client change. Mention as fallback.

 marie: Noted. I'll join their call in 20m to walk through gateway flags (disable buffering, proxy_buffering off / streaming enabled, idle timeout>=30s or heartbeat < timeout), and push server-side heartbeat patch. Will update thread after call. :thumbsup:
